b2-03-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Maybe She Is Late
b2-03-01.scenario: You are Carlos. You are waiting for Meg at a café. She is late and does not answer her phone, and you are not sure why.
b2-03-01.prompt: Tell the waiter two things that may have happened to Meg.
cues: Give one possible reason with a lo mejor
Give another possible reason with puede que
b2-03-01.target: A lo mejor se quedó dormida, o puede que esté en el autobús.
b2-03-01.english: Maybe she fell asleep, or she may be on the bus.
b2-03-01.canDo: I can use a lo mejor with the indicative and puede que with the subjunctive.

b2-03-02.title: Communicative Challenge: How Likely Is It?
b2-03-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks whether the bus will be late because of the rain. You think it is likely, but you are not sure.
b2-03-02.prompt: Tell Carlos how likely it is.
cues: Say that it is probable that the bus is late
Say that it is not certain
b2-03-02.target: Es probable que el autobús llegue tarde, pero no es seguro.
b2-03-02.english: It is probable that the bus will be late, but it is not certain.
b2-03-02.canDo: I can use es probable que and no es seguro que with the subjunctive, and es evidente que with the indicative.

b2-03-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Where Can He Be?
b2-03-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos has not answered your messages all evening. You think about what he is probably doing.
b2-03-03.prompt: Say what you think Carlos is doing.
cues: Guess what he is doing now
Guess what he has already done
b2-03-03.target: Carlos no contesta; estará trabajando o ya habrá salido de la oficina.
b2-03-03.english: Carlos is not answering; he is probably working, or he has probably left the office already.
b2-03-03.canDo: I can use the future to guess about the present, as in estará en casa.

b2-03-04.title: Communicative Challenge: What Time Was It?
b2-03-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what time it was when you got home last night. You do not remember exactly.
b2-03-04.prompt: Tell Meg what time you think it was.
cues: Say that you are not sure
Guess the time you got home
b2-03-04.target: No sé, serían las diez cuando llegué a casa.
b2-03-04.english: I don't know, it was probably about ten when I got home.
b2-03-04.canDo: I can use the conditional to guess about a moment in the past, as in serían las diez.

b2-03-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Rain or Sun?
b2-03-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what the weather will be like this weekend. You think it will rain, but the sun may come out.
b2-03-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what you think about the weekend.
cues: Say that it will most likely rain
Say that maybe the sun will come out
b2-03-05.target: Seguramente va a llover este fin de semana, pero a lo mejor sale el sol.
b2-03-05.english: It will most likely rain this weekend, but maybe the sun will come out.
b2-03-05.canDo: I can use seguramente, probablemente and sin duda to say how sure I am.

b2-03-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Did Nobody Act?
b2-03-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have read a text about a novel in which a whole town knows that something terrible will happen, and nobody stops it. Carlos asks why you think nobody acted.
b2-03-consolidation.target: Es probable que nadie lo creyera, y quizás tuvieran miedo.
b2-03-consolidation.english: It is probable that nobody believed it, and perhaps they were afraid.
b2-03-consolidation.canDo: I can say how sure I am about something in the present and in the past.
